question: How did the first wave of Kolmogorov-Arnold Network variants modify edge-function parameterization, and what evidence and unresolved engineering issues determine whether KANs are useful alternatives to MLPs?

key_findings.claim: The survey's unifying architectural distinction is that KANs learn univariate functions on edges, typically splines plus a base activation, instead of learning scalar edge weights followed by fixed node activations.
key_findings.evidence: It derives the connection to the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, then writes a multilayer KAN as sums of learned edge functions and describes the original B-spline/SiLU implementation.

key_findings.claim: The early literature rapidly diversified the edge basis and surrounding architecture rather than converging on one standard KAN.
key_findings.evidence: The taxonomy and timeline include efficient radial-basis variants, Fourier, wavelet, rational, convolutional, recurrent/time-series, graph, PDE, federated, quantum, and hybrid transformer designs, with different training and regularization choices.

key_findings.claim: Interpretability and parameter efficiency are recurring motivations, but the surveyed evidence is heterogeneous and often lacks matched strong baselines.
key_findings.evidence: Applications report inspectable learned functions or compact fits in forecasting, science, and healthcare, yet task protocols, parameter matching, hyperparameter budgets, and latency measurements differ substantially across cited papers. The survey does not conduct a cross-method replication.

anchors.section: Comparison with traditional neural architectures / Table 3

key_findings.claim: The principal unresolved risks are high-dimensional compute, spline-grid optimization, noise sensitivity, hardware inefficiency, and unclear scaling relative to tuned MLPs and transformers.
key_findings.evidence: The future-work synthesis calls for faster implementations, robust training and regularization, systematic explainability, high-dimensional benchmarks, hardware-aware variants, and stronger head-to-head evaluation.

method.core_idea: Organize the fast-growing KAN literature by learned edge-function family, surrounding network structure, training process, application, and claimed tradeoff with conventional networks.
method.mechanism: The paper introduces the theorem and base architecture, builds chronological and architectural tables of variants, then narratively reviews applications, comparisons with MLP/CNN/RNN/transformer families, training methods, interpretability, and open deployment challenges.
assumptions: The selected publications adequately represent the early KAN literature despite no formal systematic-search protocol.
Results from heterogeneous datasets and tuning budgets can be compared at a qualitative level.
The Kolmogorov-Arnold theorem provides useful architectural motivation even though it does not predict finite-sample optimization or efficiency.
Learned univariate edge functions are human-interpretable when visualized, without a task-specific user study.

techniques.role: Classifies KAN variants by spline, RBF, Fourier, wavelet, rational, and hybrid bases.
Tracks rapid extensions across sequence, graph, vision, scientific, and federated settings.
Summarizes reported tradeoffs with MLP, CNN, RNN, and transformer alternatives.
Consolidates optimization, scaling, robustness, and hardware gaps into a research agenda.

evaluations.setting: Surveyed KAN variants published through late 2024.
evaluations.metric: Coverage by basis, architecture, training method, and application domain.
evaluations.result: The tables document a broad but fragmented family spanning efficient approximations, sequences, graphs, PDEs, vision, healthcare, and communications.

evaluations.setting: Narrative comparison of KANs with MLPs, CNNs, RNNs, transformers, and Bayesian networks.
evaluations.metric: Reported accuracy, parameter use, interpretability, and computational tradeoffs in source papers.
evaluations.result: Some sources report competitive compact models, but protocols are too heterogeneous for a defensible aggregate superiority claim.
evaluations.baseline: Task-specific conventional architectures cited in the surveyed studies.

evaluations.setting: Deployment and training challenges across application studies.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative recurrence of scaling, stability, noise, and hardware concerns.
evaluations.result: Spline evaluation and grid adaptation repeatedly emerge as cost/stability bottlenecks, motivating simpler bases and hybrid designs.
evaluations.baseline: Fixed-activation dense layers with mature accelerator support.

limitations: The review does not document database queries, inclusion criteria, deduplication, or quality assessment.
It became time-bounded quickly because KAN variants appeared at high volume after the search period.
Most performance claims are inherited from source papers rather than re-evaluated under matched parameter, compute, and tuning budgets.
Interpretability is discussed largely through function plots and symbolic intuition, with limited causal or user evaluation.
failure_modes: Spline grid resolution can make KAN training unstable, memory-heavy, or sensitive to data scaling.
An expressive edge basis can overfit noise while appearing interpretable after selective visualization.
Parameter-count advantages may disappear in wall-clock time because each parameter is computationally expensive.
Hybrid variants can attribute gains to KAN layers without ablating the conventional base path.
reusable_insights: Architecture comparisons should match parameters, FLOPs, latency, tuning budget, and seed count—not parameter count alone.
Edge-function families should be treated as a design axis separate from topology and training method.
A useful KAN benchmark should jointly test predictive quality, stability, interpretability, and hardware efficiency.
open_questions: Which learned basis yields a reproducible Pareto improvement over tuned MLPs at realistic dimensionality?
Can interpretability of edge functions be validated causally and with domain experts?
What compiler and kernel designs remove the current accelerator disadvantage of KAN layers?

competitive_landscape.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces the modern learnable-edge-function KAN architecture that the survey organizes and extends.
competitive_landscape.difference: The original paper proposes and demonstrates B-spline KANs; this work is a broad taxonomy and application review rather than a new architecture.

competitive_landscape.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) for Time Series Classification and Robust Analysis
competitive_landscape.relationship: Runs a comparatively broad matched test of KAN, MLP, and hybrid structures over 128 time-series datasets.
competitive_landscape.difference: Its ablation finds the conventional base component dominates many outputs and performance is largely comparable to MLPs, providing more controlled evidence than the survey's heterogeneous claims.

competitive_landscape.title: Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks for Small Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Separates interpretability/audit claims from replacement-quality claims for KAN feed-forward layers in language models.
competitive_landscape.difference: Its multi-seed contemporary study finds useful scalar-function audits but no consistent benchmark, quality, or latency advantage over strong MLP/SwiGLU baselines, sharpening the survey's open scaling question.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: This is a comprehensive early survey of KAN foundations, variants, applications, comparisons, and future challenges.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Large chronological and architectural tables bring together many quickly diverging KAN designs and application domains.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The breadth is useful as a 2024 snapshot, but the lack of systematic-review protocol and matched evidence means it should be used as a map of claims, not evidence of KAN superiority.

reviewer_notes: Read the full 35-page survey and checked the original architecture plus two controlled follow-up studies at their primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23.
